title: "Reset this section" leaves a dial's step toggle on the step the user switched it to
repro: On dist/v6.html open Equation. Click the toggle beside Power n (id powStep): it changes from "±0.1" to "±1". Click "Reset this section" in Equation (document.querySelector('#secEq .dial-reset').click()). Read document.getElementById('powStep').textContent, then click the up arrow of Power n.
expected: After the reset the section is as the page opens it: the toggle reads ±0.1 and the up arrow takes the power from 2 to 2.1.
actual: The values go back (power 2, iterations 14) but the toggle still reads ±1, so the next press of the up arrow gives 3. Measured: opening ±0.1, after a click ±1, after Reset this section ±1.
evidence: out/t6/controls/resets.log, line "step toggle of Power n: opening ±0.1, after a click ±1, after Reset this section ±1"
suggested_fix: src/js/70-dial.js, addDial: in the control's reset() also put the step mode back to the one the dial started on (and repaint the toggle text and aria-pressed), so resetGroup and the page's Reset everything cover it. notes/fix-dial.md already lists this as not done.

title: Mandelbrot picture goes completely black when 'Orbit steps skipped at the start' is 0 with the trap as the solid
repro: python tools/shot.py --url dist/v6.html --actions out/t6/solids/pm.json (step 1). By hand on a fresh dist/v6.html in Mandelbrot mode: const $=id=>document.getElementById(id), sel=(id,v)=>{const e=$(id);e.value=String(v);e.dispatchEvent(new Event('change',{bubbles:true}));}, type=(id,v)=>{const e=$(id);e.value=v;e.dispatchEvent(new Event('input',{bubbles:true}));e.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown',{key:'Enter',bubbles:true}));}; sel('col-trap',1); sel('col-solid',1); type('col-skipNum','0');
expected: An object, as in Julia mode where skip 0 shows the trap shape plus the bubbles (out/t6/solids/p-j-skip0.png), or a dial that does not go to 0 in Mandelbrot mode.
actual: The whole stage is pure black, not even the background gradient: mean colour 0.1 of 255 against 9/13/18 normally; 0.06 % bright pixels against 13.2 % at skip 1. The dial is one notch below its starting value of 1. Tried with the cross only; probable cause (not traced): the orbit's starting point 0 is the same for every point of space and lies on the trap, so everything is solid and the camera is inside it.
evidence: out/t6/solids/p-m-skip0.png, out/t6/solids/sheet-pm.png (first tile), out/t6/solids/pm.log step 1
suggested_fix: src/js/30-shaders.js, orbitDE: in Mandelbrot mode do not count the starting value z0 toward the trap solid (begin with the first orbit point that depends on c). Or src/js/25-colour.js, COLOUR_CONTROLS key 'skip': lowest value 1 while S.mode is 'm'.

title: Trap thickness at the low end of its dial makes the solid vanish instead of thinner
repro: python tools/shot.py --url dist/v6.html --actions out/t6/solids/pj.json (steps 1 to 3) and out/t6/solids/pm.json (step 10). By hand: $('mode-j').click(); sel('col-trap',5); sel('col-solid',1); type('col-radiusNum','0.7'); type('col-thickNum','0.005'); (helpers as in solids-1). Mandelbrot: sel('col-trap',1); sel('col-solid',1); type('col-skipNum','2'); type('col-thickNum','0.01');
expected: The same chain of bubbles with thinner walls, the same cross with thinner rods: the dial's ordinary range is 0.005 to 0.5.
actual: Julia c = -1, shell 0.7: at 0.005 (the dial's lowest ordinary value) the picture is empty but for one fleck, 0.12 % bright pixels against 30.4 % at 0.05; at 0.02 the big bubble shows a washed-out patch on the sheet. Mandelbrot cross at 0.01: only a few hairlines are left, 0.77 % bright pixels. Looks like the rule that fades layers thinner than two pixels (TRAP_THIN, gPix) taking the large first pieces too.
evidence: out/t6/solids/p-j-thick0.005.png, p-j-thick0.02.png, p-m-thick0.01.png, sheet-pj.png, sheet-pm.png
suggested_fix: src/js/30-shaders.js, orbitDE, the thin layer rule (TRAP_THIN, gPix): fade only the late, fine layers, not the pieces made by the first counted steps, so a thin shell stays a thin shell. Failing that, src/js/25-colour.js 'thick': raise the lowest value and say in the help that very thin walls disappear.

title: Point (and Ray) as the solid are nearly empty pictures at the opening settings

title: Point, Line and Ray give look-alike objects: the same lace in the Kleinian view, nearly the plain set on Julia c = -1
repro: python tools/shot.py --url dist/v6.html --actions out/t6/solids/k.json and out/t6/solids/j1.json; compare k-point-s1.png, k-line-s1.png, k-ray-s1.png and j1-point-s1.png, j1-line-s1.png, j1-ray-s1.png. expected: The user's words: the shape changes with the trap selected.
actual: Kleinian: all three show the same lens-shaped slab of fine purple lace and nothing else (2.5 to 3.4 % of pixels clearly differ between them); the lace is also the body of every other Kleinian trap solid, with the trap's own pieces stuck on, and it reads as speckle at the size of the sheet (not examined at full size). Julia c = -1: all three show the plain chain of bubbles with a thin rod (5 to 5.7 % differ), because every inside orbit ends on the trap centre. With the default trap centre the user sees 'same shape, other colours' for three of the seven shapes in these pictures.
evidence: out/t6/solids/sheet-k.png, out/t6/solids/sheet-j1.png
suggested_fix: Kleinian: src/js/30-shaders.js, kde (trapSolid branch): look at why the lace does not depend on the trap and whether the thin layer rule (gPix, not built for the Kleinian solid per notes/r5-speed.md) would clear it. Julia: src/js/25-colour.js, a note for Point, Line and Ray suggesting to move the trap centre off the set's own resting points.

title: Bubbles with ragged holes at higher skips, off-centre traps and small radius
repro: python tools/shot.py --url dist/v6.html --actions out/t6/solids/pj.json (steps 7, 8, 9, 14, 15). title: The hint 'lower the iterations to keep only the large ones' changes almost nothing
repro: python tools/shot.py --url dist/v6.html --actions out/t6/solids/pj.json (steps 18 to 21) and out/t6/solids/pm.json (steps 6 to 9); compare p-j-iter3.png with p-j-iter80.png and p-m-iter4.png with p-m-iter80.png. The fine layers are already taken away by the drawing, so the dial the note points to has no visible effect; the dials that do change the object are thickness, skip, radius and centre. suggested_fix: src/js/25-colour.js, COLOUR_CONTROLS, the note with 'when: colSolidOn': replace the last clause with what works, for example 'Trap thickness, the steps skipped and the trap radius and centre change the object most.'

title: Cut face with "How deep inside" does not look like the inside of the 2D view
repro: On dist/v6.html in Mandelbrot mode, 3D: tick 'Cut the solid open at height z' (cutOn, z = 0), tick col-cutFace, choose 'How deep inside' in col-inMode, look from above (squaringLab.cam.pitch = 1.1; squaringLab.touch()). Then tick 2D view with the same inside colouring and compare.

title: Outline goes soft and its ink line vanishes when zoomed into the seahorse valley
repro: On dist/v6.html: tick 2D view; type 300 into the Iterations box (iterNum); const L = squaringLab; L.S.v2.x = -0.7453; L.S.v2.y = 0.1127; L.S.v2.h = 0.03 (then 0.003 and 0.0005); L.syncControls(); L.refresh(false); wait for L.idle(). Or run out/t6/flat/c.json, steps 1 to 10.

actual: At heights 0.03, 0.003 and 0.0005 the set is cream blobs with soft, cloud-like edges and no visible ink line. Cause not established: it may be the 300 iteration limit in that region rather than the outline code; I did not get to try more iterations.
evidence: out/t6/flat/sheet-zoom-crops.png (100% crops, left to right 3.2, 0.3, 0.03, 0.003, 0.0005); out/t6/flat/c/Z-0_03.png, Z-0_003.png, Z-0_0005.png

title: The time left is wrong by a factor of 3 to 5 at the start and goes up while the job runs
repro: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t6/export/a_sizes.py 4k   (opening settings, Save a picture: Size 3840 x 2160, Quality Fine, File type JPG, Start; the script reads #exportStep every 250 ms and prints what it said against what was true). By hand: open dist/v6.html, Save a picture, 3840 x 2160, Fine, Start, and watch the line under the bar.
expected: A time left that is roughly right and counts down.
actual: 4K Fine, 119.6 s in all: at 1 s 'About 37 seconds left' (true 119), then 29, 30, 39, 48, 55, 53, 37, 40, 43, 45, and at 107 s 'About 39 seconds left' (true 13). 8K: 32 s said at the start, 149 s true. Typed 1234 x 778: 7 s said, 19 s true. The percentage counts pixels, and the empty tiles above and below the solid draw many times faster than the tiles on it (2 to 25 % in the first 10 s, 63 to 66 % in 30 s later). Measured on the opening picture only, on the shared GPU with two other jobs of mine running; the pattern follows the rows of tiles, not the load.
evidence: out/t6/export/A-4k.log, out/t6/export/A-8k.log, out/t6/export/A-typed.log (lines 'time left' and 'said/true')
suggested_fix: src/js/45-export.js, exportRun(), function went(): the estimate assumes every pixel costs the same. Before the tile loop, time a small patch (for instance 32 x 32 at the centre) of every tile with one pass and weight each tile's share of the bar and of job.left by that cost; or at least show no time until the first tile that hits the solid is done and smooth job.left so it cannot rise.

title: After a save that throws, 'Save the file' is dead for that picture
repro: On dist/v6.html run a small job to the end (Typed 400 x 300, As on screen now), then in the console: window.squaringLabSaveHook = () => { throw new Error('no'); }; document.getElementById('exportSave').click(); then window.squaringLabSaveHook = (n, b) => console.log('got', n); document.getElementById('exportSave').click();   Or: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t6/export/runs.py refuse  (line 'D hook throws').
expected: A plain sentence that the file could not be saved, and Save the file works on the next press.
actual: The message stays 'The picture is ready.', an uncaught 'Error: hook says no' is logged from saveFile via exportSave, and the second press hands over nothing (got 0): r.saving is never cleared. Only Discard gets out. Only the test hook can throw today; the host and download paths are caught.
evidence: out/t6/export/R-refuse.log line 'D hook throws' ({"msg": "The picture is ready.", "rejections": ["hook says no"]}, then {"got": 0}); out/t6/export/D-hook-throws.png
suggested_fix: src/js/45-export.js, exportSave(): wrap the await in try/catch/finally, clear r.saving in the finally and show EXPORT_WORDS.failed-style words on a throw. The 3D model's save (src/js/46-mesh.js line 620) has the same shape. Also catch around the hook call in saveFile (src/js/00-core.js line 105).

title: "...so you can try again" is said even when trying again cannot help
repro: Fresh dist/v6.html, in the console before saving: window.claude = { use: async () => { throw new Error('no downloads'); } };  run a small job, press Save the file, read #exportMsg; press again. Or: python out/t6/export/runs.py refuse (line 'D host without downloads').
expected: When the host cannot save at all, the message says so without inviting another try; or another try really asks the host again.
actual: 'Saving files is not available in this view. The picture is still here, so you can try again.' saveFile keeps the failed answer (saveHost = null, src/js/00-core.js line 108), so every later press gives the same sentence without asking the host. The second half is reasoned from the code; the sentence is measured. The same tail follows 'The file is too large to save from here. Try a smaller size.' and 'This kind of file cannot be saved from here.'
evidence: out/t6/export/R-refuse.log, lines 'D host without downloads' and 'D host answers'
suggested_fix: src/js/45-export.js, exportSave(): add the 'try again' tail only for the codes declined and rate_limited (out.code). src/js/00-core.js, saveFile(): do not keep a failed use() (leave saveHost undefined when it throws).

title: Colours in the OBJ and PLY do not match the picture for trap-coloured Mandelbrot and Julia solids: rings and other hues
repro: Open dist/v6.html (opening state, colour by orbit trap). Console: window.squaringLabSaveHook = (n, b) => { window.zipBlob = b; }; document.getElementById('meshStart').click(); when squaringLab.meshBusy() is false: document.getElementById('meshSave').click(). Unzip, open mandelbrot-128.ply with its vertex colours and compare with the page. Or from the workspace root: python out/t6/mesh/drive.py x mandel:128 rabbit:128 julia1:128 cut:128 klein:128, then python out/t6/mesh/check.py mandel-128 rabbit-128 julia1-128 cut-128 klein-128 and look at out/t6/mesh/pics/cmp-<job>.png (left the page, middle the PLY drawn from the same camera).
expected: The model carries the picture's colours: on the opening Mandelbrot a smooth blue top with yellow and orange bands at the rim. docs/SPEC6.md says of the volume sampling: 'so a model's colours match the picture and carry no rings'.
actual: The Mandelbrot model is covered with concentric green and orange rings; the rabbit model is mostly orange with rings where the picture is cyan and green; the Julia set for c = -1 is patchy with ring patterns. The flat face of a cut solid is cream in the picture and blue to purple in the model. Median hue difference between picture and model: Mandelbrot 91.5 degrees (18% of pixels within 30 degrees), rabbit 66.3, Julia c = -1 32.5, cut 28.8; for comparison the Kleinian view 2.8 and the two trap solids 4.4 and 9.3, which do match. This is the model side of the known trap-colour item of docs/SPEC6.md; it is filed because in this build it is not cured and the rings are strong, not faint.
evidence: out/t6/mesh/pics/cmp-mandel-128.png ; out/t6/mesh/pics/sheet-cmp-a.png (Julia, rabbit, Kleinian, trap solid) ; out/t6/mesh/pics/sheet-cmp-b.png (third row: the cut face) ; numbers in out/t6/mesh/check-small.txt
suggested_fix: src/js/30-shaders.js, the raw branch (uRaw) that sampleSlice in src/js/40-render.js draws: a sample's colour is worked out at the grid point, which lies up to a cell off the surface, and the trap colouring there differs from the surface's and changes with that distance, which draws rings wherever the surface crosses grid levels. Move the point onto the surface (a few steps down the distance estimate) before colouring it, or add a call that colours given points. Then in src/js/46-mesh.js meshPoint(), colour each mesh point at its own position instead of taking the outside end of its grid edge. For the cut face decide on one colour rule and use it in both the picture and the model.

title: A negative power gives a model that does not look like the picture, and at 512 cells it crumbles into 9,901 pieces of which one wisp is kept
repro: Open dist/v6.html, type -2 into Power n (#pow) and press Enter, wait for the picture, open Save a 3D model and press Start the model at 128, then again at 512. Or from the workspace root: python out/t6/mesh/drive.py x negpow:96,128,512 then python out/t6/mesh/check.py negpow-96 negpow-128 negpow-512 --nodraw (leave out --nodraw for the pictures); with every piece kept: python out/t6/mesh/drive.py x special:edge.
expected: A model of the solid in the picture: the stack of leaves and shells around the central spine.
actual: At 128 cells the model is a thick heart-shaped band with a spine: 55.6% of the picture's outline is missing from it and the outlines overlap by only 0.32; the panel says 'The largest of 1,075'. With every piece kept the overlap is 0.56 and the model covers 73% more of the frame than the picture does (a thick outer band where the picture shows thin arcs). The volume of the kept piece is 16.8 cm3 at 96 cells, 8.3 at 128 and 0.52 at 512, where the panel says 'The largest of 9,901'. The meshes themselves are closed and valid. Not isolated: offset 0 was not tried on this picture.
evidence: out/t6/mesh/pics/sheet-cmp-b.png (first two rows) ; out/t6/mesh/log-b.txt and log-d.txt (panel facts) ; out/t6/mesh/checks/negpow-128.json, negpow-512.json, negpow-128-allpieces.json
suggested_fix: Start in src/js/46-mesh.js, meshBuild() and meshPoint(): the level o.offset * h is compared with the raw estimate, which reads far too short on this solid (see mesh-4), so thin leaves swell into a band at a coarse grid and fall apart at a fine one. Try offset 0 on this picture first; then divide the estimate by its slope between neighbouring samples before applying the level. If offset 0 still differs from the picture, the raw distance for inside-out solids in src/js/30-shaders.js (uRaw) is the cause and the defect moves to engine. In either case see mesh-3 for the missing warning.

title: 'Keep only the largest piece' (on by default) drops most of a solid made of several parts and the panel does not say how much
repro: Open dist/v6.html, tick Julia mosaic (document.getElementById('m-mosaic').click()), wait for the picture, press Start the model. Second case: Power n = -2, Start the model at 128, then untick 'Keep only the largest piece' and start again to compare the triangle counts.
expected: When the kept piece is a small part of what the picture shows, the panel says so in plain words and points to the tick box.
actual: Mosaic: the picture shows about 40 small sets, the model is one of them (4,048 triangles, 100 x 82.0 x 58.9 mm), 97.3% of the picture's outline is missing; the only hint is the row 'Pieces: The largest of 30'. title: While the graphics context is lost the status line keeps its old text and nothing says why the picture stopped
repro: Run: PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 python out/t6/walk/once.py context (parts 1 and 2). By hand on dist/v6.html: wait for the picture, run in the page: const gl = document.getElementById('view').getContext('webgl2'); window.__ext = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context'); window.__ext.loseContext(); then click Julia: the status line still reads "Done: 12 passes at 862 x 701" and the picture does not change. Then window.__ext.restoreContext(), press Fine under Quality and speed and lose the context again 0.25 s later: the status line reads "Drawing at full size" for as long as the context stays lost (checked at 0.3 s and 1.8 s).
expected: A plain sentence on the status line or the picture while the graphics are interrupted, as the picture panel has, so that a frozen picture is explained.
actual: The status line keeps its last text ("Done: ..." or "Drawing at full size"), the busy sign is off, and squaringLab.idle() reports true in the mid-draw case although nothing is being drawn. Once the context is restored everything recovers by itself (idle after 2.4 s and 8.3 s, no console problems). A real loss is rare and usually short, hence minor.
evidence: out/t6/walk/once-context.log (lines starting "1." and "2." and the two lines under each).
suggested_fix: src/js/40-render.js, the 'webglcontextlost' listener set up in initGL (it already calls stageProgress(null) and bgPump()): also call say() with a sentence such as "The graphics of this page were interrupted. The picture comes back by itself."; the 'webglcontextrestored' listener already calls touch(), which replaces the text.
